title: The Buffoon and the Countryman

full_text:
A celebrated city buffoon drew immense crowds to the theater by mimicking the squealing of a pig beneath his cloak. He squeaked, grunted, and squealed so humorously that the audience cheered and awarded him the grand prize.

A simple countryman in the crowd stood up and declared that he would compete against the buffoon the following evening.

The next day, the theater was packed. The buffoon repeated his performance and received thunderous applause.

The countryman then stepped onto the stage, wrapped in a thick cloak. He pinched a real live piglet concealed beneath his arm, causing the animal to squeal and shriek with genuine pig cries.

The audience jeered and hissed, throwing rotten fruit and shouting: "Terrible! The buffoon sounds far more like a pig than you do!"

The countryman pulled the live piglet out from under his cloak and held it high above his head: "Behold, critics! It is not me you are hissing, but the pig himself! Your prejudice prefers a counterfeit to nature's own truth!"
moral: Prejudice blinds men to genuine truth in favor of celebrated counterfeits.
